mainTitle: 🌐 Digital Omnipresence: The Systemic Surveillance Ecosystem
mainDescription: Analysis of the digital surveillance ecosystem — This article examines the surveillance and monitoring ecosystem implemented by Lusophone Wikipedia administrators and checkusers against the user WazzimaGiygg (Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres), including device fingerprinting, IMEI and MAC Address collection, cross-platform tracking, off-wiki monitoring and the creation of a digital omnipresence system for institutional persecution.
section1Title: 1. Introduction: Digital Surveillance as a Tool of Persecution
section1Text1: Digital omnipresence refers to the ability to monitor, track and identify an individual across multiple platforms, devices and contexts, creating a surveillance ecosystem that makes it impossible for the victim to escape monitoring. In the WazzimaGiygg case, administrators implemented a comprehensive digital surveillance system that included device fingerprinting, hardware data collection, tracking on social networks and forums, and off-wiki monitoring — all aimed at persecuting and neutralizing the user.

warningSurveillanceText: The WazzimaGiygg case reveals a digital surveillance ecosystem of alarming proportions. Administrators used device fingerprinting, IMEI and MAC Address collection, cross-platform tracking and off-wiki monitoring to create a digital omnipresence that made it impossible for the victim to escape persecution.
sub2_1Text1: Device fingerprinting is the collection of information about the software and hardware of a remote device for identification purposes. This technique allows identifying devices even when persistent cookies cannot be read, the IP address is hidden, or the user changes browsers on the same device.
sub2_1Text2: In the WazzimaGiygg case, device fingerprinting was used to:
fingerprintList: Identify the user even after changing accounts or browsers
Monitor hardware through IMEI and MAC Address
Create a persistent profile that cannot be erased by the user
fingerprintNoteText:
Device fingerprinting collects information such as:

• Browser configuration: Type, version, plugins, extensions
• Operating system: Type, version, settings
• Hardware: GPU, processor, screen, resolution
• Canvas fingerprinting: Graphics rendering to identify GPU
• Fonts: List of installed fonts
• Regional settings: Language, time zone, currency
• IMEI and MAC Address: Unique hardware identifiers
sub2_2Text1: IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) and MAC Address (Media Access Control address) are unique identifiers assigned to devices. The MAC Address is used in Ethernet, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth networks, while IMEI is specific to mobile devices.
imeiMacList: IMEI: Unique 15-digit number that identifies a mobile device.
MAC Address: Unique 48-bit identifier assigned to network interfaces.
Abusive use: In the WazzimaGiygg case, these identifiers were collected to monitor the user beyond the permitted scope.
LGPD violation: Collection without consent constitutes violation of Arts. 6, 7 and 42 of the LGPD.
imeiWarningTitle: ⚠️ IMEI AND MAC ADDRESS COLLECTION - SERIOUS VIOLATION:
imeiWarningText: The collection of hardware identifiers (IMEI and MAC Address) without user authorization constitutes violation of the LGPD (Arts. 6, 7, 42) and may constitute the crime of computer device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code), with a penalty of imprisonment of 1 to 4 years.

sub3_2Title: 3.2 The Device as an Extension of the Person
sub3_2Text1: As highlighted by the Wikimedia Foundation's digital security resources, "our devices are increasingly extensions of ourselves." Digital surveillance, therefore, is not just a data violation — it is a violation of the person:
deviceExtensionList: Digital identity: The device contains the person's digital identity.
Private life: The device contains private life information.
Communications: The device is the person's means of communication.
surveillanceParadoxTitle: 🎯 DIGITAL OMNIPRESENCE AS A VIOLATION OF THE PERSON:
surveillanceParadoxText: When administrators monitor a user's device through device fingerprinting, collection of IMEI and MAC Address, and cross-platform tracking, they are not just violating data — they are violating the person themselves. Digital omnipresence creates a sense of constant persecution that is a form of psychological violence.
sub4_1Text1: Administrators used cross-platform tracking techniques to connect the user's activities across different platforms:
multiplatformList: Skyscrapercity: The account "Fantasmadaserie1100" was tracked and linked to the user.
Wikimedia Commons: The account "Chadecesio" was used as "proof" for persecution.
Social networks: Monitoring of external profiles to justify sanctions.
Forums: Tracking of activities on discussion forums.
sub4_1Text2: This technique constitutes stalking (Art. 147-A of the Penal Code) and LGPD violation (Arts. 6, 7).
sub4_2Text1: Administrators extracted metadata (exif) from the user's photographs on Wikimedia Commons:
metadataList: EXIF data: Information such as date, time, location, camera used.
Use as "proof": The metadata was used to track and persecute the user.
Device intrusion: Extraction of data from files without authorization.
metadataNoteText:
The extraction of metadata (exif) from photographs without authorization constitutes:

• LGPD violation (Art. 6 - data processing without good faith)
• Device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code - data extraction without authorization)
• Stalking (Art. 147-A of the Penal Code - persecution through personal data)
sub4_3Text1: Chronus publicly confessed to conducting off-wiki monitoring of the user:
offwikiList: Public admission: Chronus admitted to monitoring the user's external profiles.
Wikihounding: Obsessive monitoring to justify arbitrary sanctions.
Psychological violence: The feeling of being constantly monitored causes psychological harm.
Stalking configured: Repeated persecution constitutes the crime of stalking.

surveillanceCrimeText:
The surveillance ecosystem implemented against WazzimaGiygg constitutes multiple crimes:

• Stalking (Art. 147-A of the Penal Code) - repeated persecution
• Device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code) - data collection without authorization
• Criminal association (Art. 288 of the Penal Code) - coordination between agents
• LGPD violations (Arts. 6, 7, 42, 46) - unlawful data processing

surveillanceParadoxBoxText:
The digital surveillance implemented against WazzimaGiygg creates a perverse paradox:

• The platform that should protect privacy violates privacy
• The tools that should prevent abuse are used to abuse
• Knowledge that should be free becomes controlled knowledge
• The community that should be participatory is silenced

This paradox reveals the corruption of the free knowledge ideal.

section8Title: 8. 📢 Recommendations for Protection against Digital Surveillance
platformRecommendations: Prohibition of Device Fingerprinting: Strict policy against hardware data collection.
Limitation of Collected Data: Collect only what is strictly necessary.
Transparency: Inform users about what is collected and why.
Consent: Obtain explicit consent for any data collection.
Limited Retention: Delete data after the legal period (90 days for IPs).
Prohibition of IMEI/MAC Collection: Hardware identifiers cannot be collected.
Surveillance Audit: Periodic review of monitoring tools and practices.
adminRecommendations: Tool Limitation: CheckUser should only be used for platform protection.
Prohibition of Off-wiki Monitoring: Do not track users outside the platform.
Prohibition of Wikihounding: Do not obsessively pursue users.
Respect for Privacy: Handle personal data with due care.
Consequences for Abuses: Penalties for administrators who abuse surveillance tools.
userRecommendations: Fingerprinting Test: Use tools like EFF's Panopticlick to test vulnerability.
Secure Browsers: Use browsers with fingerprinting protection (Firefox, Brave).
Privacy Extensions: Use Privacy Badger and other privacy extensions.
Awareness: Know the risks of digital surveillance.
section9Title: 9. 📢 Call to Action: End of Abusive Digital Surveillance
callToActionList: Criminal Investigation: Opening of police inquiry to investigate the crimes of device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code) and stalking (Art. 147-A of the Penal Code).
Civil Investigation: Civil action for moral and material damages against all agents involved.
Notification to ANPD: Formal complaint for LGPD violations (Arts. 6, 7, 42, 46).
Notification to WMF: Formal communication about the abuse of surveillance tools.
Demotion: Removal of all involved agents from administrative positions.
Prohibition of Device Fingerprinting: Implementation of strict policy against hardware data collection.
Surveillance Audit: Review of all monitoring tools and practices.
User Protection: Guarantee that users will not be abusively monitored.
section10Title: 10. Conclusion: Digital Omnipresence as a Weapon of Persecution
finalText1: The WazzimaGiygg case reveals the creation of a digital surveillance ecosystem of alarming proportions. Administrators used device fingerprinting, IMEI and MAC Address collection, cross-platform tracking, off-wiki monitoring and metadata extraction to create a digital omnipresence that made it impossible for the victim to escape persecution.
finalText2: The implemented digital surveillance is not just a data violation — it is a violation of the person. The constant monitoring of the victim's device, activities and life constitutes stalking and device intrusion, in addition to multiple LGPD violations.
finalText3: Digital omnipresence is a weapon of persecution that must be combated with legal, administrative and technological measures. Protection against abusive digital surveillance is a fundamental right that must be guaranteed to all users.
